chunks: And it was narrated from Ismāʿīl ibn Muslim that he asked al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام:
About the salat (prayer) behind a man who denies the decree of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. He said: "He should repeat every salat (prayer) that he performed behind him."

key_terms.اَلصَّادِقَ: Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, the one answering the legal question
key_terms.اَلصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), specifically congregational prayer performed behind an imam
key_terms.بِقَدَرِ: the divine decree or determination of Allah
key_terms.خَلْفَهُ: behind him, meaning behind that prayer leader
key_terms.رَجُلٍ: a man acting as the prayer leader
key_terms.لِيُعِدْ: he must repeat or perform again

ai.seo_question: Must a person repeat salat (prayer) performed behind someone who denies Allah's decree?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning salat (prayer) performed behind a person who rejects the divine decree of Allah. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام instructs that such prayers must be repeated, showing the significance of the imam's sound creed in congregational prayer.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1116 - It was narrated from Isma'il ibn Muslim that he asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as)

about praying behind a man who denies (or rejects) the decree (Qadar) of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic.
He (Al-Sadiq) replied: "He should repeat every prayer he performed behind him”.
